paragraphs.title: The Power of Speech and Wisdom

easy.explanation: Proverbs 15:1 says, “A soft answer turneth away wrath.”
easy.q: What does a soft answer turn away?
What do grievous words stir up?

easy.explanation: The LORD’s eyes are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
easy.q: What are the eyes of the LORD beholding?

answers: The wise use knowledge aright, while fools pour out foolishness
The wise seek riches, while fools seek poverty
The wise remain silent, while fools pray
medium.explanation: The tongue of the wise uses knowledge properly, but fools pour out foolishness.
medium.q: How are the speech of the wise and the mouth of fools contrasted?

medium.explanation: A wholesome tongue is described as a tree of life.
medium.q: What is a “wholesome tongue” compared to?

answers: Speech can wound or damage a person inwardly
Riches are more important than words
People are not responsible for their speech
medium.explanation: Perverseness in the tongue is compared with a breach in the spirit.
medium.q: What does “a breach in the spirit” suggest in this passage?

answers: Speech can influence both people and situations
challenge.explanation: A soft answer calms wrath, and wise speech uses knowledge properly.
challenge.q: What common lesson is shown by a soft answer and the tongue of the wise?

answers: Nothing is hidden from His sight
Only the wise are seen by Him
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the eyes of the LORD are in every place.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the LORD beholding both the evil and the good?

answers: Someone who speaks gently and receives instruction
Someone who pours out foolishness and rejects correction
Someone who increases anger through harsh speech
challenge.explanation: The passage commends wise, wholesome speech and attentive correction.
challenge.q: Which person best reflects the teaching of these verses?

short_answers.question: According to Proverbs 15:1, what turns away wrath?
short_answers.explanation: A soft answer turns away wrath.

short_answers.question: What does a wholesome tongue resemble?
short_answers.explanation: The verse compares a wholesome tongue to a tree of life.

short_answers.question: Whom do the eyes of the LORD behold?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD sees both the evil and the good.

easy.explanation: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD.
easy.q: What is the sacrifice of the wicked to the LORD?

easy.explanation: The prayer of the upright is the LORD’s delight.
easy.q: What is the prayer of the upright to the LORD?

easy.explanation: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge.
easy.q: What does the heart of a person with understanding seek?

answers: The scorner rejects reproof, while the discerning person seeks knowledge
The scorner seeks knowledge, while the discerning person rejects correction
Both reject every kind of counsel
medium.explanation: The passage describes one who dislikes reproof and another whose heart seeks knowledge.
medium.q: What is the difference between a scorner and a discerning person?

answers: Something especially desired by the LORD
medium.explanation: The sacrifice and way of the wicked are described as abominations.
medium.q: What does “an abomination unto the LORD” mean in these verses?

answers: It belongs to those who live uprightly rather than wickedly
It is offered only by wealthy people
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the prayer of the upright with the sacrifice of the wicked.
medium.q: Why is the prayer of the upright pleasing to God?

answers: Rejecting correction leads to death, while receiving it gives understanding
challenge.explanation: Those who hate reproof shall die, while the one who hears it gains understanding.
challenge.q: What connection do the verses make between reproof and life?

answers: God distinguishes between conduct He rejects and conduct He loves
All ways are equally acceptable to God
The verses refer only to physical roads
challenge.explanation: The LORD abhors the way of the wicked but loves the person who follows righteousness.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between the way of the wicked and following righteousness?

answers: The wicked are rejected, the scorner rejects reproof, and the understanding person seeks knowledge
The wicked seek knowledge, the scorner accepts correction, and the wise reject it
All the people are described alike
challenge.explanation: These verses develop a series of contrasts between wickedness, scorn, and understanding.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the people in this passage?

short_answers.question: What is the prayer of the upright to the LORD?
short_answers.explanation: The prayer of the upright is the LORD’s delight.

short_answers.question: What does the understanding heart seek?
What happens to the person who hates reproof?
short_answers.explanation: Proverbs 15:10 says that he who hates reproof shall die.

paragraphs.title: Poverty, Joy, and Peace at Home

easy.explanation: The merry-hearted person has a continual feast.
easy.q: What does a person with a merry heart have?

answers: Little with the fear of the LORD
easy.explanation: Little with the fear of the LORD is better than great treasure and trouble.
easy.q: What is better than great treasure and trouble?

easy.explanation: A wrathful man stirreth up strife.
easy.q: What does a wrathful man stir up?

answers: Love is better than abundance accompanied by hatred
Meat is always better than vegetables
medium.explanation: A dinner of herbs with love is better than a stalled ox with hatred.
medium.q: What is the contrast between a dinner of herbs and a stalled ox?

medium.explanation: The way of the slothful is compared to a hedge of thorns.
medium.q: What is an “hedge of thorns” used to describe?

medium.explanation: The person who is slow to anger appeases strife.
medium.q: How does being slow to anger affect strife?

answers: Spiritual reverence and loving relationships are better than outward abundance
Happiness depends only on the amount of food
challenge.explanation: Both verses value reverence and love over wealth accompanied by trouble or hatred.
challenge.q: What principle connects little with the fear of the LORD and a meal where love is present?

answers: Laziness creates obstacles, while righteousness makes the way plain
Righteousness is always more difficult than laziness
A person’s character has no connection with his path
challenge.explanation: The slothful way is like thorns, while the righteous way is made plain.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between the slothful person’s way and the righteous person’s way?

answers: Anger and hatred produce strife, while love and cheerfulness bring joy
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts wrath and hatred with love, cheerfulness, and patience.
challenge.q: How do these verses connect a person’s character with the atmosphere around him?

short_answers.question: What is better than great treasure and trouble?
short_answers.answer: Little with the fear of the LORD
short_answers.explanation: The verse says that little with the fear of the LORD is better.

short_answers.question: What is better than a stalled ox with hatred?
short_answers.answer: A dinner of herbs where love is
short_answers.explanation: Love makes the simple meal better than abundance with hatred.

short_answers.question: What does a slow-tempered person appease?
short_answers.explanation: He that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

easy.q: What happens to purposes without counsel?

easy.explanation: In the multitude of counsellors purposes are established.
easy.q: What happens in the multitude of counsellors?

easy.explanation: The way of life is above to the wise.
easy.q: Where is the way of life to the wise?

medium.explanation: The verse calls a word spoken in due season good.
medium.q: What is good about a word spoken in due season?

answers: A person who covets profit and troubles his own house
A person who refuses all gifts for righteousness
medium.explanation: The greedy person troubles his own house through the pursuit of gain.

answers: He turns it into a palace
medium.explanation: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud.
medium.q: What does the LORD do to the house of the proud?

answers: Wise consultation helps establish sound plans
It is always best to decide alone
challenge.explanation: Purposes fail without counsel but are established with many counselors.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between no counsel and many counsellors teach?

answers: The passage places pleasant words alongside God’s protection of the widow
The widow is presented as a threat to pure speech
Pure words are connected only with wealth
challenge.explanation: The verses mention pleasant words and the LORD establishing the widow’s border.
challenge.q: How are pure words related to justice for the vulnerable?

answers: Careful answers and concern for the vulnerable
challenge.explanation: The passage condemns pride and greed while commending counsel and fitting speech.
challenge.q: Which conduct most opposes the teaching of these verses?

short_answers.question: What establishes purposes according to Proverbs 15:22?
short_answers.explanation: Purposes are established in the multitude of counsellors.

short_answers.question: Where is the way of life to the wise?
short_answers.explanation: The way of life is above to the wise.

short_answers.question: What happens to the house of the proud?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud.

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Heart and Human Prayer

easy.explanation: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer.
easy.q: What does the heart of the righteous study?

easy.explanation: The mouth of the wicked pours out evil things.
easy.q: What does the mouth of the wicked pour out?

easy.explanation: A good report maketh the bones fat.
easy.q: What does a good report make fat?

answers: He is far from the wicked but hears the prayer of the righteous
He is far from the righteous but hears the wicked
medium.explanation: The LORD is far from the wicked but hears the prayer of the righteous.
medium.q: What is the difference between the LORD’s attitude toward the wicked and the righteous?

medium.explanation: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart.
medium.q: What does “the light of the eyes” do?

answers: So that his answer may be thoughtful rather than evil
So that he can avoid all speech
So that he can pour out foolishness
medium.explanation: The righteous heart studies to answer, in contrast with the wicked mouth.
medium.q: Why does the righteous person study before answering?

answers: Both describe an inward character that produces acceptable speech or prayer
challenge.explanation: The righteous person thinks carefully and is heard when he prays.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the righteous heart and the prayer of the righteous?

answers: Pleasant appearances or news can bring joy and strength
challenge.explanation: Both expressions describe something that refreshes and encourages.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from placing the light of the eyes beside a good report?

answers: Someone who thinks before answering and brings good news
Someone whose mouth produces evil and ignores prayer
Someone who increases anger and hatred
challenge.explanation: The verses commend thoughtful answers, righteous prayer, and good reports.
challenge.q: Which person best fits the whole passage?

short_answers.question: What does the righteous heart study?
short_answers.explanation: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer.

short_answers.question: Whose prayer does the LORD hear?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD hears the prayer of the righteous.

short_answers.question: What makes the bones fat?
short_answers.explanation: A good report maketh the bones fat.

easy.explanation: The ear that hears the reproof of life abides among the wise.
easy.q: What does the ear that hears reproof of life do?

easy.explanation: He that hears reproof gets understanding.
easy.q: What does a person gain by hearing reproof?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “before honour is humility.”

answers: Correction that leads toward a wise and fruitful life
medium.explanation: The passage presents reproof as instruction that leads to life and wisdom.

answers: The person who hears reproof gains understanding and remains among the wise
Hearing reproof makes a person a scorner
Reproof has no connection with wisdom
medium.explanation: Those who hear reproof gain understanding and abide among the wise.
medium.q: How are hearing reproof and wisdom connected?

medium.explanation: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom.
medium.q: What is the fear of the LORD called in the final verse?

answers: Hearing reproof, gaining understanding, fearing the LORD, and practicing humility
Pride, rejecting correction, riches, and honour
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from listening to correction to wisdom, reverence, and humility.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in the closing verses?

answers: Receiving correction is connected with belonging among wise people
Listening to reproof removes a person from wisdom
challenge.explanation: The verse places the receptive listener among the wise.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “abideth among the wise”?

answers: The verse presents humility as preceding or preparing a person for honour
The verse denies any relationship between humility and honour
Honour is presented as the cause of pride
challenge.explanation: The order of the words teaches that humility comes before honour.
challenge.q: Why is humility placed before honour?

short_answers.question: What does the person who hears reproof get?
short_answers.explanation: He that heareth reproof getteth understanding.

short_answers.question: What is the fear of the LORD?
short_answers.explanation: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom.
